Summary Description: Dr. Elizabeth A. Karr specializes in bacterial transcriptional regulation with a strong emphasis on integrating structural biology and bioinformatics to delineate regulon architecture and regulatory networks. Her work spans determining DNA-binding specificities of response regulators like RR_1586 in C. difficile through bacterial one-hybrid screens, motif discovery, and cross-species conservation analyses, to structural characterization of PadR-family transcription regulators and their DNA-binding modes. She employs a comprehensive toolkit—ranging from MEME/RSAT-based motif analyses and GLAM2 motif discovery to EMSAs and GFP-based in vivo validations, and culminating in high-resolution X-ray crystallography—to elucidate autoregulatory loops, phosphorylation- and oligomerization-dependent regulation, and broader regulatory dynamics relevant to pathogen virulence and stress responses. Her research exemplifies a rigorous, multi-layered approach to decoding transcriptional control in bacteria and demonstrates methodological innovation in marrying computational predictions with experimental verification and structural insights.
